data.turoyo: U ṭʕono di naḥšo du miṯo b ġer dukoṯo kmaḥtile baʕ ʕarabat, sədayna lo, lašan d oṯe l bole da nsanat, i naqqa d ṭoʕən ḥa, d oḏəʕ, kaʔinnahu huwe ste, kətle yawmo, gməṭʕən hawxa ʕal ak katfoṯo w gədəzze huwe ste, gməqwər, lašan d huyoleyo b bole dayəm, d huyoleyo l qul ʕayne xd u məre.
data.translation: Das Tragen der Bare des Toten ... anderswo legen sie (den Sarg) in ein Fahrzeug, doch bei uns nicht, damit sich die Leute erinnern ... wenn jemand (den Sarg) trägt, weiß er, dass es auch für ihn einen Tag gibt, an dem auch er so auf den Schultern getragen wird und auch er begraben wird. Damit es ihm immer im Sinn ist, damit es ihm vor Augen steht wie ein Spiegel.

rationale: Thin Detransitive Infectum cell; generic future burial with patient subject and no agent.

summary: 49 occurrences reviewed. qwərre, qwəḷḷan, qwullilux and qwəlle show different l-series agent sequences and assimilation; do not infer a new stem from r/l or emphatic spelling. qwirənne and qwərulle require separate object analysis.

The Detransitive Infectum presents the patient without an expressed agent, both in a general funeral reflection and an episcopal burial plan. Part. Pass. qwiro is also an established disparaging epithet, including direct address and demonstrative qwirano.

Burial wishes range from affectionate survival formulas (quratli, Qurət emux) to curses and self-imprecations. These speech acts do not require new lexical senses of burying. One blessing is added under Idiomatic phrases after search.

PrS 85/64 liya w lu taʕlo can name l-marked agents of qwərulle; this is not automatically a coordinated patient phrase. Repeated qawrulle after a singular washing actor (PrS 52/59, 52/103) may instead have indefinite plural buriers.

Purpose d- clauses do not themselves assert completed burial (PrS 38/23; PrS 52/59). Talay 1/81 has a prohibition repeated as the desired content; neither second-person directive is an Imperativ box solely because it addresses listeners.

Existing examples at JL 16.7.29, 25/46, 35/68, 67/9 and 76/167 are retained without duplicate additions. Existing active examples with no printed number are semantically within the single active sense 1.

All qwarṯo/qwarṯayḏe tokens are the same feminine burial-event noun, including funeral attendance and səmalle qwarṯo. File provisionally as Nomen Actionis rather than duplicating active and Detransitive Infinitiv boxes on identical noun forms. This does not establish a productive infinitival paradigm.
qwərwolle provides active Preterit-wa after round 1; active qwərre and qəwrilan remain ordinary burial. The reduced vowel and l-series assimilation are source forms, not new stems.
Literal qwiro at Jan 3.27/653 is distinguished from the disparaging Part. Pass. epithet assigned to D2 in round 1. Jan adds no evidence for a further curse sense.
Round 1 already fills active Preterit and Infectum beyond five contexts. Do not add repeated funerals solely on the reader's counts from the old entry.
Confirm the affectionate versus complaining force of quratli in Bilgic Hochzeit und Tod/19, and compare the hostile optatives and self-curse.
Confirm object/agent segmentation in qwərulle (PrS 48/24, 85/64), qawratte (57/31) and qwirənne (74/146).
Are the buriers in PrS 52/59 and 52/103 indefinite 3pl despite the singular washing actor?
Check transmitted hato for the male rider at 67/32 without normalizing its gender.
Is qwarṯo a productive Nomen Actionis or a lexical burial/funeral noun? Its repeated event reference supports provisional inclusion; it supplies no Detransitive distinction.
Jan 2.7/1886 Ayko qwərwo: confirm Detransitive Preterit-wa, a reduced form of qwirwo, or an elliptical active form. The one question and machine translation do not securely establish the box.
Correct Erzboschof to Erzbischof
rationale: The German title is misspelled; the supplied translation at 35/68 reads Erzbischof.
